info.name: Microsoft Fabric REST API
info.description:
Sample collection for the Microsoft Fabric workshop. Demonstrates listing workspaces, creating a workspace, importing an item, assigning a role (ACL) on a workspace, and retrieving an item's definition.

## Setup
1. Get a Fabric access token. Easiest options:
   - Azure CLI: `az account get-access-token --resource https://api.fabric.microsoft.com --query accessToken -o tsv`
   - PowerShell (Az): `(Get-AzAccessToken -ResourceUrl https://api.fabric.microsoft.com).Token`
2. Open the collection's **Variables** tab and paste the token into `accessToken`. Also fill in `capacityId`, `principalId`, etc.
3. Run the requests in order — IDs returned by **Create Workspace** and **Import Item** are stored back into the collection variables `workspaceId` and `itemId` automatically via test scripts.

Tokens are short-lived (~1 hour). When requests start returning 401, grab a fresh token and update the variable.

variable.description: Bearer token for the Fabric API. Get one with `az account get-access-token --resource https://api.fabric.microsoft.com --query accessToken -o tsv`.

request.description: Returns all Fabric workspaces accessible to the authenticated principal.
Creates a new workspace and assigns it to the configured Fabric capacity. The new workspace ID is stored in the `workspaceId` collection variable by the test script.
Grants the specified principal (user, group, or service principal) the chosen role on the workspace. Roles: Admin | Member | Contributor | Viewer.

exec: console.log('Long-running operation accepted. Poll the Location header for completion before reading itemId.');

request.description: Creates an item in the workspace by importing its definition inline. The example imports a minimal Notebook (`print("Hello Fabric")`). Replace `type`, `format`, `path`, and the base64 `payload` to import other item types (e.g. SemanticModel, Report, DataPipeline). Long-running creates return 202 with a `Location` header to poll.

Returns the full definition (parts + base64 payloads) of the specified item. May return 202 with a `Location` header for long-running operations — poll until the operation completes, then GET the result URL.
